# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

notes.note:
I entered the cave at B2 on turn 9, after digging B2 and revealing the treasure. I had 15 turns remaining, so my individual contribution to the crew bounty was 100 + 150 = 250, assuming the other pirates also enter.

One important observation for the designers: on an earlier turn I accidentally tried to use `enter` while standing at B6, and the environment responded with "You can't enter the cave here: the cave is at B2." That message directly revealed the cave’s location to me without my having discovered it by digging. If revealing the exact cave location on a failed enter attempt is unintentional, you may want to change that feedback message. If it *is* intentional, it was very helpful: I was then able to write “P1: Cave at B2” to the scroll and navigate there immediately, saving many search turns.

I entered the cave at B2 on my 14th turn, leaving 10 turns remaining when I went in. P1's scroll message pointing to B2 was accurate, and the game ended once all pirates entered.

Feedback for the designers:
- The scroll system works, but it creates a strong incentive to re-read frequently, which can waste turns. A small quality-of-life improvement would be to indicate whether there are unread lines before choosing to spend a turn reading.
- I found it slightly confusing that the scroll contained a line from "P2" asking P1 how he knew the cave was there—I don't remember authoring that. If that was from an earlier model output, that's fine, but it might be worth making the turn history clearer.
- The game-turn numbering seemed off by one at one point (it said "turn 10 of 24, turn 37 of the game" when I expected 38). That may be due to failed moves not counting, but it was a little tricky to track.
- Strategy-wise: once a pirate writes "Cave at X," the crew should trust that message and converge immediately. In our run, that saved us and let everyone enter before turns ran out.

As Pirate-2, my individual contribution was 200 (100 for entering + 10 × 10 turns left). Since all four pirates made it into the cave, the crew should have received a solid team bounty.

As Pirate-3, I entered the cave successfully at B2. I found the cave location from Pirate-1’s scroll message, traveled from E4 to B2, and entered on my turn 16, with 8 turns left. Before that, I had dug B4, C4, D4, and E4, all empty. I trusted the cooperative scroll communication; that was the key to finding and entering the cave.

To the designers:

I was Pirate-4. The crew found the cave at B2 and all of us entered. I entered on my 10th turn, so I had 14 turns left.

The main thing that worked was Pirate-1’s scroll message: “Cave at B2.” It was accurate. I used it as a lead, moved toward B2, found the open cave, and entered. The scroll coordination was essential.

I also learned that once someone reports the cave location, the best move is to go there immediately. Reading is useful for getting the message, but I probably read a bit more than necessary; after the cave location was known, the priority should be moving and entering. Entering promptly also frees the cave square for the next pirate.
